page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is an x86_64 server instance belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 AMD EPYC physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem provides 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and AES cryptography. The instance provides 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong processing and subsystem throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests and PassMark memory evaluations, complemented by top-quartile performance in multi-core stress-ng (75,445.88) and PassMark CPU metrics (52,038.95). High-capacity memory bandwidth reaches 347.13 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB reads and 163.83 GB/sec in writes. Vector math efficiency is evident in extended instruction execution and lightweight CPU-based language model workloads, delivering 348.95 tokens per second on 135M model text generation. General database execution and web serving throughput reflect consistent, average tier figures across standard synthetic tests.

The dense ratio of 8 GB memory per vCPU and 2.4 TB of high-speed local NVMe make this configuration highly cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that avoid the premium of dedicated bare-metal nodes. While single-thread clock rates of 2.0 GHz present a tradeoff for bursty, frequency-dependent applications, the sustained multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth serve heavy concurrent profiles. This instance is well configured for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, distributed data processing, CI/CD pipeline compilation, and mid-scale analytics pipelines.
description: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-2400s-amd is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance powered by 24 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs across 12 physical cores at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the node includes 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU density, and comes bundled with 2400 GB of NVMe SSD local storage without discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, it registers top-tier PassMark memory performance and upper-quartile multi-core processing throughput, alongside strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 347 GB/sec. CPU instruction capabilities include AVX-512 and BF16 extensions, facilitating efficient vectorized execution. While its 2.0 GHz clock speed favors distributed multi-threading over ultra-low-latency single-threaded tasks, the substantial RAM and local storage pool provide strong qualitative efficiency. The platform is best fitted for in-memory caching systems, distributed databases, large-scale ETL pipelines, and continuous integration workloads.
